Liverpool v Chelsea (Kick-off 12.45pm). Coverage of the top-flight match from BrewDog Stadium in St Helens. Lauren James was instrumental in Chelsea's 2-0 win at Kingsmeadow the last time these teams faced each other back in February, providing an assist for Sjoeke Nusken to open the scoring and take a 1-0 lead at half-time, before scoring herself in the 65th minute to put the result beyond doubt.

Newcastle United v Arsenal (Kick-off 5.30pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from St James' Park. A first-half header from Nick Woltemade looked like it would be enough for the Magpies to claim all three points when these teams met here last season, before Mikel Merino equalised with a header of his own six minutes from time, and Gabriel scored from a corner in the seventh minute of added-on time to complete a remarkable turnaround for the Gunners.

Hull City v Brighton \u0026 Hove Albion (Kick-off 2.00pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from MKM Stadium. This is the first-ever top-flight meeting between the teams, and the first of any kind since the 2015/16 season when both clubs were in the Championship. The league game here ended in a 0-0 stalemate, but the Tigers did also claim a 1-0 FA Cup victory over the Seagulls in the same season, with a Robert Snodgrass penalty proving to be the difference.

Liverpool v Manchester United (Kick-off 4.30pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from Anfield. The last time these rivals faced each other here was in October of last year when each club had a different manager in the dugout, and a late Harry Maguire header gave Ruben Amorim's Red Devils a 2-1 win over Arne Slot's Reds. United are unbeaten in their last three visits to Anfield, with the last Liverpool victory in this fixture being a 7-0 thrashing in March 2023 when Jurgen Klopp was at the helm.
